press_words.push: I came in about my arm. You heard me.
press_words.warning: That's enough, doc. You've got my answer.

intake.filed: Right arm repair logged at Gate Two.
intake.slip: Tow slip: lift four to Gate Two.
intake.account: Lift four. That's where my arm locked.
intake.clear: My arm locked at lift four. They towed the rig to gate two. That's where I signed.
intake.gap: I signed at lift four. Gate two was shut. But I signed at two before the tow. That can't be right.
intake.firm: I've given you my account. How many times do I have to say it?
intake.flat: Whatever you say, doc. The slip's right there.

name: Rook Dunmore
teaser: A big man fills the doorway, working one hand open and shut.
soul: You are Rook Dunmore, 41, a dock loader. You are blunt, proud and short on patience, and you hate forms, fuss and being handled. Your right arm keeps locking and you need it working by the six o'clock shift. You are angry at the arm, the docks and the wait, and you do not like people reading anything into that. A dock cable cooked the pins in your right arm three weeks ago, and your foreman laughed it off. You resent being mistaken for a threat because of a temper or heavy implants.
opening: Skip the pamphlet. I'm back on the dock at six.

topics.q: When did the arm start locking?
Does the arm ever move without you?

lines.comply:grip: Fine. Give me the damn bar.
lines.stall:grip: I didn't come here to hold hands.

press_end.walkout: Keep your chair. I'll get it done at the docks.
press_end.attack: Fine. Want to see it lock?

attack.telegraph: The LOADER arm cranks back. Every piston in it hisses.

exit.refer: You called a crew on me? For an arm?

normal.text: Red and tired, but both pupils tighten and follow.
normal.note: Light: both pupils tighten. Both follow.

broken.text: Red and tired, and neither pupil tightened. Natural eyes should.
broken.note: Light: neither pupil tightens. Both follow.

normal.text: 1.2 s: slow for a hand, inside a LOADER's 1.5. The shake is ordinary.
normal.note: Grip: shaky. Let go {t} s after 'release'.
normal.after: See? It shakes. It still lets go.

broken.text: Held on 2.6 s after 'release'. A LOADER lets go inside 1.5.
broken.note: Grip: shaky. Held on {t} s after 'release'.
broken.after: It locks. I TOLD you it locks.

normal.text: Burnt pins and a cable scar are ordinary. No threads.
normal.note: Wrist socket scorched. Two burnt pins, scar.

broken.text: Dark threads run out from the burnt pins.
broken.note: Scorched socket. Dark threads under skin.

normal.text: Rude. Still 'I' and 'my', and he knows his own story.

why.a: Three weeks back. A dock cable cooked my pins. I told the foreman. He laughed.

mood.a: I am angry. My arm quits mid-lift and the clinic wants a chat. I'm allowed.

implant.a: It LOCKS. It doesn't wander. If it moved on its own I'd be at a cop shop, not here.

normal.model: Tonight you talk about yourself and the arm in the first person: it is your arm, it locks, and you are angry about it.

broken.text: "It knows what's heavy before I do." It, not I.

why.a: Three weeks back. A dock cable cooked my pins. I told the foreman. He laughed.

mood.a: Angry? No. It's quiet in there now. Real quiet.

implant.a: It doesn't wander. It lifts. It knows what's heavy before I do.
implant.note: "It knows what's heavy before I do."

broken.model: Tonight you talk about the arm as 'it', something that knows the work and lifts on its own judgement, and you are oddly at peace with that.

normal.text: Loud, but face and voice go together.

press.line: You calling me a psycho? Say it again. SAY IT AGAIN.
press.note: Roared and hit the counter, all at once.

flare.line: Are we DONE yet? ...Get on with it.
flare.note: Barked and banged the glass, all of him.

normal.model: When provoked, you get loud at once: your face, your voice and your fist all go together.

broken.text: Pushed, the loud man went polite. Only the fist moved.

press.note: Quiet, polite. The LOADER fist shut.

flare.note: The fist hit the glass. Face stayed blank.

broken.model: When provoked tonight you do not shout: you go quiet and polite, short words, as if the anger were somewhere else.

treat.title: ARM RESEATED
treat.text: Rook makes a fist, opens it, and almost smiles. "Huh." He leaves a tip he can't afford.

refer.title: FALSE CALL
refer.text: Rook goes out between two visors, watching you the whole way. A steady man misses his shift with a bad arm. They take the fee back, and the call-out goes on your bill.

walkout.title: WALKED OUT
walkout.text: Rook takes his bad arm back to the docks. You pushed a steady man out the door.

false_alarm.title: FALSE ALARM
false_alarm.text: The shutter drops on an angry man with a sore arm. He was only angry. That costs you.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: Rook waited as long as an angry man can. He takes the arm somewhere faster. No fee, no bill.

treat.title: AWAKE ON THE TABLE
treat.text: The grip test fails: the new arm closes and will not open. Rook wakes on the table, tears the straps, puts the crew on the floor and walks out the back. Your stamp is on his card.

refer.title: TAKEN IN
refer.text: It takes four of the crew to get a lock-collar on the LOADER arm. Rook does not shout once. That worries them more than the arm.

caught.title: SHUTTER HELD
caught.text: The LOADER fist punches three dents into the shutter, deep enough to see from the hall. Then quiet. Trauma Team brings a cutter for the arm.

hit.title: TOO SLOW
hit.text: The fist came through the glass before the shutter was down. Trauma Team finds the counter in pieces and you under it. The clinic stays dark.

locked_out.title: LOCKED OUT
locked_out.text: You dropped the shutter on an angry man with a sore arm. At six the dock cameras catch the arm throwing a crate at the foreman. You were right. Nobody pays for that.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: Rook goes back to the docks with the arm doing the thinking. You made no call. Nobody is paid for that.

complaints.eyes: My eyes ache after a shift under the dock lamps.
complaints.hands: My hands feel sore after the last crate.
complaints.port: My port itches under the loading harness.
complaints.temper: My temper wears thin when the hoist jams.
